transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my breathing, mainly when I go up the stairs. I've been getting out of breath climbing them, and it's been getting worse over the last three months or so.
Could you tell me how bad your breathing has been and how much it’s affecting your daily life, and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?

I have to stop halfway up the stairs to get my breath back — it's 14 stairs — whereas I used to manage the whole flight without stopping. It's mainly stairs and walking uphill, and it settles after I rest for two or three minutes; I'm fine when I'm sitting still. As for allergies, I don't have any that I know of — no bad reactions to medicines.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started recently, and also anything about your past health — like other conditions you've had, operations, or hospital stays?

I take rivaroxaban 15 mg once a day with my evening meal, bisoprolol 5 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 2.5 mg once a day. As for my health, I've had atrial fibrillation for about five years and I had a heart attack twelve years ago. I also had a heart scan at the hospital last year, but I'm afraid I can't remember what the result was.
Have you had any other symptoms along with getting out of breath?
Yes, my ankles tend to get a bit puffy in the evening, and I've started using two pillows at night instead of one. I've not had any chest pain, and no cough or blood, and no fever either.
When you get out of breath, where in your body do you feel it most — and does it stay in one spot or spread anywhere else?
It's not really in one spot — I just feel generally puffed out and can't get enough air in. It doesn't spread anywhere, and it's not a pain at all.
Are there any other medicines you take, either regularly or that you've started recently?
No, that's the lot — those four are the only ones I take. I haven't started anything new recently.
What's worrying you most about all this, and what are you hoping we can do for you today?
What worries me most is managing the stairs to get to bed — the bedroom's upstairs and I'm having to stop halfway. And really, I want to know whether my heart is getting worse.
Is there anything else about your past health — such as other long-term conditions, operations, or hospital stays — that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else — just the atrial fibrillation and the heart attack, and that heart scan last year. I can't think of any other conditions or operations.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed that seems to come along with the breathlessness, or anything else you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else I've noticed. Just the puffy ankles in the evening and needing the extra pillow.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
